papers.title_in_file: Quantum algorithms: A survey of applications and end-to-end complexities
papers.version_note: Same paper (arXiv 2310.03011), a later version than the 2023 date in the file name; the text calls itself a snapshot of the state of play in roughly mid-2024. The record id says 2025.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, the Section 9 (machine learning with classical data) introduction, and the start of Section 9.5 (quantum neural networks and kernels). The other 400 or so pages were not read.
papers.what_it_is: A 416-page survey of quantum algorithm primitives and application areas that tracks end-to-end resource costs and compares against classical methods.

assertions.value: The authors state that their evaluation suggests few of the considered quantum machine learning algorithms show any promise of quantum advantage in the immediate future, citing data loading, tomography and classical dequantized algorithms as factors.
quotes: At present, our evaluation suggests that few of the considered quantum machine learning algorithms show any promise of quantum advantage in the immediate future.
issues of loading classical data into the quantum device and extracting classical data via tomography
assertions.certainty_reason: The survey authors' own assessment, stated as provisional.

assertions.value: The authors state that for quantum neural networks there are currently no practical use cases with full end-to-end performance guarantees, and that quantum neural networks and quantum kernel methods contain heuristic elements that make concrete analytic end-to-end resource estimates challenging.
assertions.anchor: Section 9 introduction, p. 157, and Section 9.5, p. 190
quotes: there are currently no practical use cases with full end-to-end performance guarantees in the same way that we have for other quantum algorithms
contain heuristic elements which make it challenging to perform concrete analytic end-to-end resource estimates
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' assessment of the field; no new result.

assertions.value: The authors state that the survey does not attempt to advance the state of the art, and that because of a general lack of application-scale experimental data it focuses on provable speedups and mentions NISQ algorithms only in passing.
quotes: this survey does not attempt to advance the state of the art; rather, it aims to collect, synthesize, and contextualize key results in the literature
we focus on elucidating provable speedups, and we only mention noisy, intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) algorithms in passing
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope.

assertions.value: The authors state that the current literature generally lacks fully end-to-end analyses for concrete quantum applications.
quotes: An overarching takeaway of this survey is that the current literature generally lacks fully end-to-end analyses for concrete quantum applications.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' overarching assessment of the literature.

papers.what_it_is: A review of quantum neural networks on gate-based quantum computers for molecular property prediction and molecular generation in drug discovery.

assertions.value: The authors state that the hardware and algorithmic challenges for QML are substantial, and that the requirements for coherence, qubit connectivity, and state preparation introduce significant hurdles that have yet to be fully overcome.

assertions.value: The authors state that barren plateaus occur when the loss differences used to compute quantum weight gradients exponentially vanish with the size of the system, and that the parameter-shift method is expensive, requiring at least 2M quantum circuits for M trainable parameters.
quotes: Barren plateaus occur when the loss differences used to compute quantum weight gradients exponentially vanish with the size of the system.
expensive as it requires running at least 2M quantum circuits for M trainable parameters

papers.title_in_file: Advances in Quantum Deep Learning: An Overview
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section 4 (start, input representation), Section 6 and Section 7 (Conclusion). Sections 2, 3 and 5 were skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A survey of proposed quantum neural network schemes, quantum convolutional variants, and quantum-inspired classical deep learning methods, with no new experiments.

assertions.value: The authors state that the paper reviews and summarises the different schemes proposed to model quantum neural networks (QNNs) and other variants such as quantum convolutional networks (QCNNs).
quotes: we review and summarise the different schemes proposed to model quantum neural networks (QNNs) and other variants like quantum convolutional networks (QCNNs)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope.

assertions.value: The authors state that the majority of related works focus on the immediate benefits derived from QNNs over classical data, and that one popular strategy, binarizing each input component through a threshold, leads to a high loss of information contained in the data.
quotes: the majority of related works shift their focus to the immediate benefits derived from QNNs over classical data
This approach leads to a high loss of information contained in the data.
assertions.certainty_reason: Survey authors' characterisation of the literature.

assertions.value: The authors state that Wiebe et al. showed that quantum computing can provide a more comprehensive framework for deep learning than classical computing.
quotes: showed that quantum computing can provide a more comprehensive framework for deep learning than classical computing
assertions.certainty_reason: Result the survey attributes to another paper.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Annealing vs. QAOA: 127 Qubit Higher-Order Ising Problems on NISQ Computers
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, the first part of the results (D-Wave device comparison) and Section 4 Discussion. The circuit-construction details were skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A hardware comparison of quantum annealing on D-Wave devices against QAOA on a 127-qubit IBM device, with simulated annealing as a classical baseline, on random higher-order Ising instances.

assertions.value: The authors report that quantum annealing found higher quality solutions to the random higher-order Ising test instances than short-depth QAOA with p = 1 and p = 2, with reasonably fine grid searches over the QAOA angles and annealing schedules with pauses, and that dynamical decoupling lets 2-round QAOA marginally outperform 1-round QAOA.
quotes: We find that QA outperforms QAOA on all problem instances.

Quantum annealing finds higher quality solutions to the random test Ising models with higher order terms compared to the short depth QAOA p = 1 and p = 2 circuits, with reasonably fine grid searches over the QAOA angles and quantum annealing schedules with pauses.
We also find that dynamical decoupling enables 2-round QAOA to marginally outperform 1-round QAOA
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one hardware study on one class of instances.

assertions.value: The authors report that simulated annealing is comparable to the quantum annealing distributions, performing marginally better than them.
quotes: Simulated annealing is comparable to the quantum annealing distributions, with simulated annealing performing marginally better than the quantum annealing distributions.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: Read with the abstract's claim that QA beats QAOA, this places both quantum methods at or below the classical baseline on these instances.

assertions.value: The authors state that QAOA was run on an ensemble of random Ising instances using all 127 programmable superconducting transmon qubits of ibm washington, that how QA and QAOA scale to large system sizes is not fully understood, and that more detailed benchmarking against state of the art classical solvers is left to future work.
assertions.anchor: Abstract, p. 1; Introduction, p. 1; Section 4, p. 11
quotes: using all 127 programmable superconducting transmon qubits of ibm washington
of how both QA and QAOA will scale to large system sizes is currently not fully understood
We leave more detailed benchmarking against state of the art classical solvers on these Ising model instances to future work.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup and limits.

papers.version_note: File name says 2024; the text is arXiv 2411.09131 v3 dated 15 Dec 2025, matching the record id year 2025.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section 5.1 (decoding), Section 7 (Outlook) and Section 8 (Conclusion). Sections 2, 3, 4 and 6 were skimmed by heading.
papers.what_it_is: A multi-author review (NVIDIA-led) of how AI methods are applied across the quantum computing stack, from device design to error correction and postprocessing.

assertions.value: The authors state that the surveyed research demonstrates that AI can play a role in designing qubits, preparing efficient quantum algorithms, controlling and calibrating the device, correcting errors in realtime, and interpreting the output from QC.
quotes: The research surveyed in this review demonstrates that AI can play a role in everything from designing qubits, preparing efficient quantum algorithms, controlling and calibrating the device, correcting errors in realtime, and interpreting the output from QC.
assertions.certainty_reason: Review authors' synthesis; the underlying results are other groups' work. Several authors are NVIDIA employees.

assertions.value: The authors state that the first application of attention-based transformer models to decoding was presented in 2023, producing a logical error rate below baselines given by MWPM and Union Find decoders.
quotes: The first application of attention-based transformer models to decoding was presented in 2023, producing a logical error rate below baselines given by MWPM and Union Find decoders [149].
assertions.certainty_reason: Result the review attributes to a cited paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that many applications of AI models for quantum computing must be trained on large, high quality data sets, which often entails experimental data from quantum systems that is costly to obtain given the limited availability and capabilities of current quantum processors.
quotes: Many applications of AI models for quantum computing must be trained on large, high quality data sets.
This often entails experimental data from quantum systems, which is costly to obtain given the limited availability and capabilities of current quantum processors.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' stated obstacle; no measurement.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Approximate Optimization via Learning-based Adaptive Optimization
papers.version_note: Same paper (arXiv 2303.14877). The file is v3 (9 Mar 2024) with the shorter title shown; the file name carries the earlier title with 'Error-mitigated' and the year 2023. The record id year 2024 matches this version.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Sections 2.1 to 2.2 (start), Section 2.4 (hardware) and Section 3 Discussion. Methods and supplementary material were not read.
papers.what_it_is: A Bayesian-optimization method (DARBO) for tuning QAOA circuit parameters, tested in simulation on MAX-CUT and on a five-qubit superconducting device with error mitigation.

assertions.value: The authors report numerical results in which their DARBO optimizer for QAOA greatly outperforms conventional optimizers in terms of speed, accuracy, and stability; the exact-simulation comparison used n = 16 w3R graphs, with Adam and COBYLA as the comparison optimizers.
assertions.anchor: Abstract, p. 1; Section 2.2, Fig. 2 caption, p. 5
quotes: Our numerical results demonstrate that the algorithm greatly outperforms conventional optimizers in terms of speed, accuracy, and stability.
All the optimizations are performed on n = 16 w3R graphs.
Adam (in blue color), COBYLA (in red color), and DARBO
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on one graph family.

assertions.value: The authors state that the hardware demonstration is a proof of concept in which QAOA is implemented and evaluated on a real superconducting quantum processor using five qubits, and that scaling QAOA on real hardware with meaningful accuracy needs more pruning, compiling and error mitigation techniques in future work.
quotes: QAOA is implemented and evaluated on a real superconducting quantum processor using five qubits

To successfully scale the QAOA program on real quantum hardware with meaningful accuracy, more pruning and compiling techniques for QAOA deployment, as well as more error mitigation techniques, can be utilized in future works.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup and limits.

assertions.value: The authors report that on hardware the optimization results combined with quantum error mitigation are much better than the raw evaluations, and that a deeper QAOA with p = 2 gives a better approximation of the QUBO objective than a shallow QAOA with p = 1.
quotes: The optimization results combined with QEM are much better than the raw evaluations
Still, we show that a deeper QAOA with p = 2 gives a better approximation of the QUBO objective than a shallow QAOA with p = 1
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one five-qubit hardware experiment.
